title: Legislative districts of Laguna

{{Short description|Legislative Districts of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Laguna''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Laguna (province)|Laguna]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]], [[#2nd District|second]], [[#3rd District|third]], and [[#4th District|fourth]] congressional districts. [[File:Laguna Congressional Districts.svg|thumb|Legislative districts of Laguna.]] The component cities of [[Biñan]], [[Calamba, Laguna|Calamba]], and [[Santa Rosa, Laguna|Santa Rosa]], while remaining integral parts of the province, granted their separate congressional representations in 2015, 2018, and 2019, respectively. They later gained representation in the provincial board in 2024. == History == Laguna initially elected [[#1898–1899|four representatives, at large]], to the [[Malolos Congress]] in [[1898 Philippine legislative election|1898]]. It was later divided into two representative districts in 1907 for the [[Philippine Assembly]].{{cite PH act|chamber=Act|number=1582|date=January 9, 1907|url=https://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l5054|title=An Act to Provide for the Holding of Elections in the Philippine Islands, for the Organization of the Philippine Assembly, and for Other Purposes|accessdate=September 4, 2022}} When seats for the [[Senate of the Philippines|upper house]] of the [[Philippine Legislature]] were elected from territory-based districts between 1916 and 1935, the province formed part of the [[Philippines's 4th senatorial district|fourth senatorial district]] which elected two out of the 24-member senate. By virtue of Executive Orders No. 84 and 103 issued by [[Philippine Executive Commission]] Chairman [[Jorge B. Vargas|Jorge Vargas]] in 1942, the municipality of [[Infanta, Quezon|Infanta]] (including what is now [[General Nakar]] and [[Real, Quezon|Real]]) and the [[Polillo Islands]] were transferred to Laguna's jurisdiction, a setup which only lasted for the duration of the [[World War II|Second World War]]. [[#1943–1944|Two delegates]] represented the expanded province in the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was the [[Governor of Laguna|provincial governor]] (an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]]), while the other was elected through a provincial assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]]. [[San Pablo, Laguna|San Pablo]], being a chartered city, was [[Legislative district of San Pablo|represented separately]] in this short-lived legislative body. Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945, the province retained its two pre-war representative districts. The province was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IV-A]] from 1978 to 1984, and elected [[#1984–1986|four representatives, at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Laguna was reapportioned into four [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|congressional districts]] under the new Constitution{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|access-date=June 13, 2016}} which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, and elected members to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. The passage of Republic Act No. 10658{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=10658|title=AN ACT SEPARATING THE CITY OF BIÑAN FROM THE FIRST LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT OF THE PROVINCE OF LAGUNA TO CONSTITUTE THE LONE LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT OF THE CITY OF BIÑAN|date=March 27, 2015|access-date=June 13, 2016|author=Congress of the Philippines|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2015/03/27/republic-act-no-10658/}} on March 27, 2015 separated from the [[#1st District|first]] district the city of [[Biñan]], which first elected its [[Legislative district of Biñan|separate representative]] beginning in the [[2016 Philippine general election|2016 elections]]. However, for the purposes of electing [[Sangguniang Panlalawigan]] members, Biñan remains part of the province's [[Laguna Provincial Board#1st District|1st Sangguniang Panlalawigan District]].{{cite web|title=Resolution No. 9982 - Annex B|author=COMELEC|date=August 18, 2015|access-date=June 13, 2016|url=http://www.comelec.gov.ph/php-tpls-attachments/2016NLE/Resolutions/res9982annexB.pdf}} The passage of Republic Act No. 11078{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=11078|title=AN ACT OF SEPARATING THE CITY OF CALAMBA FROM THE SECOND LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT OF THE PROVINCE OF LAGUNA TO CONSTITUTE THE LONE LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT OF THE CITY OF CALAMBA|date=September 24, 2018|access-date=May 9, 2019|author=Congress of the Philippines|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2018/09/24/republic-act-no-11078/}} on July 23, 2018 separated from the [[#2nd District|second]] district the city of [[Calamba, Laguna|Calamba]], which elected its [[Legislative district of Calamba|separate representative]] beginning in the [[2019 Philippine general election|2019 elections]]. However, for the purposes of electing [[Sangguniang Panlalawigan]] members, Calamba remains part of the province's [[Laguna Provincial Board#2nd District|2nd Sangguniang Panlalawigan District]].{{cite web|title=Resolution No. 10434 - IN THE MATTER OF THE IMPLEMENTING RULES AND REGULATIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11078 ENTITLED, "AN ACT SEPARATING THE CITY OF CALAMBA FROM THE SECOND LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT OF THE PROVINCE OF LAGUNA TO CONSTITUTE THE LONE LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT OF THE CITY OF CALAMBA"|author=COMELEC|date=October 15, 2018|access-date=May 9, 2019|url=http://comelec.gov.ph/?r=2019NLE/Resolutions/res10434}} The passage of Republic Act No. 11395{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=11395|title=An Act Separating the City of Santa Rosa from the First Legislative District of the Province of Laguna to Constitute the Lone Legislative District of the City of Santa Rosa|date=August 28, 2019|access-date=September 13, 2019|author=Congress of the Philippines|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/downloads/2019/08aug/20190822-RA-11395-RRD.pdf}} on August 28, 2019 separated from the [[#1st District|first]] district the city of [[Santa Rosa, Laguna|Santa Rosa]], which first elected its [[Legislative district of Santa Rosa|separate representative]] beginning in the [[2022 Philippine general election|2022 elections]]. However, for the purposes of electing [[Sangguniang Panlalawigan]] members, Santa Rosa remains part of the province's [[Laguna Provincial Board#1st District|1st Sangguniang Panlalawigan District]]. In 2024, the lone congressional districts of [[legislative districts of Biñan|Biñan]], [[legislative districts of Calamba|Calamba]], and [[legislative districts of Santa Rosa|Santa Rosa]] were granted separate representations in the [[Laguna Provincial Board]] effective 2025.{{cite news|url=https://opinyon.net/national/2-board-members-for-laguna-s-districts|title=2 board members for Laguna's districts|author=OpinYon News Team|website=OpinYon News|accessdate=October 17, 2024|date=August 19, 2024}} == Current districts == The province was last redistricted in 2021, wherein the [[Legislative districts of Santa Rosa|legislative district of Santa Rosa]] was created out of the 1st district. The province's current congressional delegation composes of four members. All incumbent representatives are part of the majority bloc. {{Color box|{{party color|Lakas-Christian Muslim Democrats}}|border=darkgray}} [[Lakas–CMD]] (3)
